full_text_en:
Jiangsu Lixiahe Regional Agricultural Science Research Institute v. Baoying County Tianbu Agricultural Materials Management Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of a new plant variety right

Ruling Summary

The principle of exhaustion of rights in intellectual property law means that after a patentee, trademark owner, copyright owner, or other intellectual property right holder produces or manufactures the protected product themselves, or authorizes another to do so, and sells the product, the use or sale of such product by a third party does not constitute infringement. The exhaustion of rights doctrine is a limitation on the exercise of intellectual property rights, intended to prevent the creation of excessive monopolies that would hinder the free circulation of products in the market and affect the development and progress of social production. It also serves to protect others' lawful exercise of their own legally owned property rights. China applies the exhaustion of rights doctrine to the protection of new plant variety rights. Where another person lawfully obtains the propagating material of a new plant variety as a commodity on the market and subsequently sells or uses it, such act does not constitute infringement.

Plaintiff: Jiangsu Lixiahe Regional Agricultural Science Research Institute, domiciled at: Weiyang District, Yangzhou City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Ma Tanbin, Director of the Institute.

Defendant: Baoying County Tianbu Agricultural Materials Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Anyi Town, Baoying County, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Liu Hongyou, Chairman of the Company.

The Plaintiff, Jiangsu Lixiahe Regional Agricultural Science Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute), brought an action against the Defendant, Baoying County Tianbu Agricultural Materials Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianbu Company), for infringement of a new plant variety right before the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province.

The Plaintiff Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute alleged: The Plaintiff obtained three "New Plant Variety Right Certificates" for "Yangmai 11," "Yangmai 13," and "Yangmai 16" issued by the Ministry of Agriculture of the People's Republic of China on September 1, 2003, and November 1, 2005, respectively, with certificate numbers No. 20030407, No. 20050654, and No. 20050663, all naming the Plaintiff as the variety rights holder. On September 21 and 22, 2007, the Defendant Tianbu Company and its legal representative Liu Hongyou purchased wheat seeds "Yangmai 11" in the amount of 49,500 jin at a unit price of RMB 1.05/jin, totaling RMB 51,975; "Yangmai 11" in the amount of 30,000 jin at a unit price of RMB 1.10/jin, totaling RMB 33,000; "Yangmai 13" in the amount of 40,000 jin at a unit price of RMB 1.15/jin, totaling RMB 46,000; and "Yangmai 16" in the amount of 10,000 jin at a unit price of RMB 1.20/jin, totaling RMB 12,000, from Rudong County Seed Company, Zhongjiang Seed Industry Taixing Shennong Seed Direct Sales Outlet, and Gaoyou Zhouxiang Township Agricultural Technology Station, respectively. The total purchase of wheat seeds was 129,500 jin, totaling RMB 142,975. Subsequently, the Defendant sold the aforementioned wheat seeds at its agricultural materials chain stores located in Baoying. The Defendant's sales activities affected the sales plan of the Plaintiff and its licensee, Yangzhou Fengbao Seed Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fengbao Company), for the "Yangmai series" new plant varieties (wheat seeds) in the Baoying area, causing a decline in their sales volume. To protect the lawful rights and interests of the variety rights holder, the Plaintiff requested the court to order the Defendant to: 1. Immediately cease the infringing act of selling the propagating material of the plant varieties over which the Plaintiff enjoys the new plant variety right without the Plaintiff's permission; 2. Compensate the Plaintiff for losses in the amount of RMB 150,000; and 3. Bear the litigation costs of this case.

The Defendant Tianbu Company argued: 1. The Plaintiff Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute is not a proper party, as the Plaintiff has exclusively licensed its new plant variety rights to Jiangsu Jintudi Seed Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jintudi Company); 2. The Plaintiff's new plant variety rights have been terminated; 3. The Defendant possesses legal qualifications and may engage in relevant agricultural materials purchase and sale activities; the purchased wheat seeds have a lawful source; the Defendant has not infringed the Plaintiff's new plant variety rights; 4. The Plaintiff's claim for RMB 150,000 in damages has no legal basis.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court found the following facts at first instance:

On July 22, 2002, the Plaintiff Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute and Nanjing Agricultural University jointly filed an application with the Ministry of Agriculture of the PRC for a new plant variety right for common wheat "Yangmai 11," which was granted on September 1, 2003, under variety right number CNA20020140.9, with a protection term of 15 years. On August 27, 2003, and November 4, 2003, the Plaintiff filed applications with the Ministry of Agriculture for new plant variety rights for common wheat "Yangmai 13" and "Yangmai 16," which were both granted on November 1, 2005, under variety right numbers CNA20030316.3 and CNA20030436.4, respectively. The protection term for both varieties is 15 years. On June 29, 2004, Nanjing Agricultural University, as the co-holder of the "Yangmai 11" variety right, authorized the Plaintiff to organize, implement, and maintain the related work for the "Yangmai 11" new plant variety right, with expenses to be borne by the Plaintiff and benefits from rights enforcement to belong to the Plaintiff, and authorized the Plaintiff to unify civil, administrative, and other litigation activities as the right holder.

On January 1, 2006, the Plaintiff Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute licensed Jintudi Company to exclusively exploit the new plant variety rights for "Yangmai 11," "Yangmai 13," and "Yangmai 16." The license term was from the date of grant to December 31, 2007.

On July 3, 2007, Jintudi Company and Fengbao Company entered into a contract for the purchase and sale of crop seeds regarding "Yangmai 11" and "Yangmai 16" seeds. At the same time, Jintudi Company and Fengbao Company also signed an agreement for regional agency and sales management for Yangmai varieties in Baoying County, stipulating that Fengbao Company would be the exclusive agent for the sale of "Yangmai 11" and "Yangmai 16" seeds packaged in special packaging provided by Jintudi Company within the jurisdiction of Baoying County, Jiangsu Province, with the agency term from July 3, 2007, to December 30, 2007. The parties also agreed on liability for breach of contract as follows: "If Fengbao Company fails to exercise adequate management and control, resulting in low-price sales or unauthorized transshipment outside the jurisdiction of Baoying County, it shall compensate Jintudi Company for the economic losses caused thereby, calculated based on the quantity and price of the seeds sold at reduced prices or transshipped, and shall also pay RMB 500,000 in compensation. If Jintudi Company fails to exercise adequate management and control, causing confusion in the market supply channels or prices, Fengbao Company has the right to claim compensation for lost profits from Jintudi Company. If other agents transship seeds into Fengbao Company's agency area, Jintudi Company will assist Fengbao Company in compensating Fengbao Company with the corresponding rebates from the transshipping party based on the quantity transshipped."

On September 21, 2007, the Defendant Tianbu Company purchased 30,000 jin of "Yangmai 13" and 10,000 jin of "Yangmai 16" from Rudong County Seed Company. On September 22, 2007, the Defendant purchased 49,500 jin of "Yangmai 11" and 40,000 jin of "Yangmai 13" from Zhongjiang Seed Industry Taixing Shennong Seed Direct Sales Outlet and Gaoyou Zhouxiang Agricultural Technology Station, respectively. All the wheat seeds purchased were in special packaging provided by Jintudi Company. Subsequently, the Defendant sold the purchased wheat seeds in the Baoying area.

On December 13, 2007, Jintudi Company agreed that the Plaintiff Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute could, in the name of Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute, pursue tort liability against others in the Baoying area for infringement of the new plant variety rights for "Yangmai 11" and "Yangmai 16."

It was further found that the Defendant Tianbu Company was established on July 23, 2004, with registered capital of RMB 800,000, and its business scope includes operating a chain of agricultural materials stores with "Jiangsu Tianbu Organic Agricultural Technology Development Co., Ltd." for the sale of packaged crop seeds that are not further repackaged, as well as the sale of agricultural film, agricultural machinery, agricultural and sideline products, flowers, and seedlings, and providing agricultural technology information services.

The disputed issues at first instance were: 1. Whether the Plaintiff Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute had the proper standing to sue; 2. Whether the Defendant Tianbu Company's sales activities infringed the Plaintiff's new plant variety rights.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held at first instance:

1. According to relevant legal provisions, the owner of a new plant variety right or an interested party may file a lawsuit with a People's Court if they believe their new plant variety right has been infringed. The Plaintiff Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute and Nanjing Agricultural University are co-owners of the "Yangmai 11" variety right. Nanjing Agricultural University expressly authorized the Plaintiff to exercise rights externally in its own name and to obtain benefits, therefore the Plaintiff is entitled to exercise the new plant variety right for "Yangmai 11." Meanwhile, the Plaintiff is the variety rights holder for "Yangmai 13" and "Yangmai 16," and is entitled to exercise these two new plant variety rights. Although the Plaintiff has exclusively licensed the involved new plant variety rights to Jintudi Company for exploitation, the Plaintiff, as the owner of the involved new plant variety rights, has the right to exercise procedural rights as the rights holder when it believes its new plant variety rights have been infringed. Even if an exclusive license is granted to Jintudi Company, this does not affect the Plaintiff's ability to exercise procedural rights as the new plant variety rights holder. In summary, the Plaintiff has standing to sue. The Defendant Tianbu Company's argument that the Plaintiff is not a proper party to this lawsuit and that its rights have terminated after granting an exclusive license to Jintudi Company lacks factual and legal basis and is not adopted.

2. The purchase and sale activities of the Defendant Tianbu Company did not infringe the Plaintiff Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute's involved new plant variety rights. Article 6 of the *Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties* of the PRC provides: "The entity or individual that has completed the breeding shall enjoy an exclusive right in respect of the authorized variety. No entity or individual may, without the permission of the owner of the variety right, produce or sell the propagating material of the authorized variety for commercial purposes, or repeatedly use the propagating material of the authorized variety for the production of propagating material of another variety for commercial purposes, unless otherwise provided in these Regulations." The legislative purpose of this provision is only to protect the initial production and sale of the variety by the new plant variety right holder. That is, the new plant variety right holder has the right to produce, sell, or authorize others to produce and sell the propagating material of the authorized variety, and also has the right to prohibit others from producing or selling it for commercial purposes without permission. For the propagating material of a new plant variety that has been produced and sold by the new plant variety right holder or by an authorized person with the right holder's permission, because it has lawfully entered the stream of commerce, according to the "exhaustion of rights principle" in intellectual property law, once the new plant variety right holder has placed the authorized variety and its propagating material produced by itself or under its license on the market, its exclusive right to sell is deemed "exhausted." When another person lawfully obtains the propagating material of the authorized variety as a commodity on the market and subsequently sells or uses it, this does not constitute infringement. Based on the facts of this case, the "Yangmai 11," "Yangmai 13," and "Yangmai 16" wheat seeds purchased by the Defendant from Rudong County Seed Company and others were in special packaging indicating they were authorized for sale by the Plaintiff's licensee and came from a lawful source. Furthermore, according to Article 29, Paragraph 2 of the *Seed Law of the PRC*, which provides that "a seed operator who exclusively deals in packaged seeds that are not further repackaged, or who sells seeds on behalf of a seed operator with a seed operation license under a written entrustment, may be exempt from obtaining a seed operation license," the Defendant's act of selling seeds without further repackaging does not violate the law. Therefore, the Defendant's argument that it has legal qualifications and may engage in relevant seed purchase and sale activities should be accepted. The Defendant's act of lawfully obtaining "Yangmai 11," "Yangmai 13," and "Yangmai 16" wheat seeds on the market and then reselling them is not subject to the prohibitive rights arising from the new plant variety rights. The Defendant's above-mentioned acts did not infringe the Plaintiff's new plant variety rights. The Plaintiff's claims lack factual and legal basis and are not supported.

Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 29, Paragraph 2 of the *Seed Law of the PRC* and Articles 6 and 39 of the *Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties*, rendered the following judgment on June 20, 2008:

The claims of the Plaintiff Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute are dismissed.

Court costs of RMB 3,300 for this case shall be borne by the Plaintiff Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute.

Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Jiangsu High People's Court. The main grounds for appeal were: The first-instance judgment's finding that the *Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties* only protects the initial act of production and sale is incorrect. The principle of exhaustion of rights in the field of intellectual property law is not applicable to new plant variety rights; otherwise, the system of protection for new plant varieties would become ineffective. The Appellant requested the revocation of the first-instance judgment and a corrected judgment according to law.

The Appellee Tianbu Company argued: The exhaustion of rights principle should apply to new plant variety rights. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be upheld.

The Jiangsu High People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The disputed issue at second instance was: Whether the Appellee Tianbu Company's sales activities infringed the Appellant Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute's involved new plant variety rights, and whether the exhaustion of rights principle applies to the protection of new plant variety rights.

The Jiangsu High People's Court held at second instance:

The issue of whether the Appellee Tianbu Company's sales activities constitute infringement is essentially the issue of whether the exhaustion of rights principle in the field of intellectual property law applies to the protection of new plant variety rights. The so-called exhaustion of rights principle means that after a patentee, trademark owner, or copyright owner, or other intellectual property right holder has sold a product which it manufactured or authorized another to manufacture, the use or sale of such product by a third party is not deemed infringement. The exhaustion of rights doctrine is a limitation on the exercise of intellectual property rights. As a type of right regime in the field of intellectual property, new plant variety rights also involve the issue of exhaustion of rights. That is, after the propagating material of an authorized variety sold by the new plant variety right holder or sold with its consent is sold, its exclusive right to sell is deemed "exhausted." When another person lawfully obtains the propagating material of the authorized variety on the market and subsequently sells or uses it, this does not constitute infringement. First, the protection of the new plant variety right holder's initial act of production and sale already enables the right holder to realize its rights. After the new plant variety right holder exclusively produces and sells the propagating material of the authorized variety in accordance with the law, it has obtained the economic benefits it deserves from such exclusive production and sale activities. Once the authorized propagating material has been lawfully placed on the market, another person's subsequent sale or use of that propagating material no longer requires the permission or authorization of the new plant variety right holder and does not constitute infringement. The application of the exhaustion of rights principle to new plant variety rights is a limitation on the exercise of rights by the right holder, intended to prevent the creation of excessive monopolies that would hinder the free circulation of products in the market and affect the development and progress of social production. It also serves to protect others' lawful exercise of their own legally owned property rights. Second, Article 142, Paragraph 2 of the *General Principles of Civil Law of the PRC* clearly stipulates that if any international treaty concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China contains provisions differing from those of the civil laws of the People's Republic of China, the provisions of the international treaty shall prevail, unless the provisions are those on which the People's Republic of China has declared reservations. Article 16 of the *International Convention for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants* (1978 Act), to which China acceded in 1998, provides: "Notwithstanding the provisions of Articles 6 to 15, any Contracting Party may, in its national law, provide that the breeder's right does not extend to acts concerning any material of the variety, or of any variety covered by the provisions of Article 14(5), which has been sold or otherwise marketed by the breeder or with his consent in the territory of that Contracting Party, or any material derived from the said material, unless such acts involve: (i) further propagation of the variety, or (ii) export of material of the variety enabling its propagation, into a country which does not protect varieties of the plant genus or species to which the variety belongs, except where the exported material is for final consumption." This provision clearly indicates the application of the exhaustion of rights principle in the field of new plant variety rights. Therefore, it must be determined that China applies the exhaustion of rights principle to the protection of new plant variety rights. The Appellant Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute's contention that, after the sale of the involved new plant variety propagating material, the Appellee Tianbu Company could not commercially sell the said propagating material without its authorization, and that doing so would constitute infringement for which liability must be borne, lacks legal basis and is not supported. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be upheld.

Accordingly, the Jiangsu High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*, rendered the following judgment on October 27, 2008:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

Court costs of RMB 3,300 for the second instance shall be borne by the Appellant Lixiahe Agricultural Research Institute.

This judgment is final.
